messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SEV2 — inference-pool evictions detected in us-west-2 (multiple NotReady nodes)
Alex: grabbing pager, on my way. any known deploys?
Oncall-1: not seeing a deploy in the last 30m in deploy logs. metric spike looks like kubelet flapping + container restarts.
Alex: ok adding context — Dashboard: 3% global 99p latency bump, 0.7% increase in 5xx for generation endpoints. Dedicated customers seeing reroutes to other regions.
Oncall-1: collecting kube state now. `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-usw -o wide` output:
```
NAME             STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
infer-node-41    Ready      gpu      12d   v1.24
infer-node-42    Ready      gpu      12d   v1.24
infer-node-43    NotReady   gpu      6d    v1.24
infer-node-44    NotReady   gpu      6d    v1.24
infer-node-45    Ready      gpu      3d    v1.24
```
Oncall-1: kubelet logs from infer-node-43 show repeated restart loop: `systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited` then `kernel: NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup` and driver errors referencing CUDA. grabbing journalctl.
Oncall-1: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 on infer-node-43:
```
Mar 10 12:02:03 infer-node-43 kubelet[1234]: E03010 12:02:03 server.go:123] failed to start kubelet: error creating device plugin: plugin crashed: exit status 1
Mar 10 12:02:05 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 10 12:02:06 kubelet[1234]: kubelet: peer closed connection
Mar 10 12:02:09 kubelet[1234]: Container runtime error: containerd: starting container: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:xxx: while setting up sandbox: rootfs: failed to mount ...: invalid argument
```
Alex: that Xid 79 = GPU reset / driver crash. looks like driver / firmware instability => nodes go NotReady, then kubelet restarts cascade.
Mira: are multiple AZs affected or just us-west-2a?
Kevin: only us-west-2a so far, 43/44 are colocated hardware racks. suspecting a host-level thermal/firmware event.
Jaya: traffic impact: routing logs show automatic smart-routing moved ~12% of inference traffic to eu-west and us-east. latency impact concentrated for small-token chat flows.
Support-Bot: opened support tickets for three Dedicated customers flagged by rate-limiter: ticket#RDW-8731, RDW-8732, RDW-8733. notifying CS.
Oncall-1: mitigation plan — isolate faulty nodes, cordon + drain, scale up spare pool, restart node drivers/power-cycle via BMC if needed. will also kick fallback model policy for critical routes.
Alex: commands to run: `kubectl cordon infer-node-43 && kubectl drain infer-node-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` then `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=infer-node-43` to confirm evictions.
Oncall-1: starting drains now. evicting pods from infer-node-43...
Oncall-1: drain complete for infer-node-43. pods rescheduled to infer-node-45 and autoscaled spare nodes.
deploy-bot: Autoscaler: scaled deployment inference-pool-usw from 8 -> 12 replicas to absorb evicted work.
Mira: can we put a taint on the rack to prevent scheduling until infra confirms drivers patched? `kubectl taint nodes infer-node-43 key=hardware:NoSchedule`
Kevin: infra asked for BMC power-cycle on both 43/44 to attempt NVidia driver recovery. submitting access now.
Alex: customer impact summary for on-call handoff: 
- Affected region: us-west-2a only
- Symptom: node-level GPU driver crashes (NVRM Xid 79) -> kubelet restart -> NotReady -> pod evictions
- Impact: ~3% global 99p latency, 0.7% increased 5xx; Dedicated customers had transient reroutes, no data loss reported
- Mitigation applied: cordon+drain nodes 43/44, autoscaler bumped pool, fallback model variant for lowest-latency routes enabled, infra powercycled hosts, tainted nodes to avoid reschedule
Jaya: logs show one pod failed with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` before container restart — suggests memory/driver mismatch rather than pure heat. need to capture GPU diagnostics after power-cycle.
Kevin: BMC indicates both hosts rebooted at 12:18Z. kernel logs post-boot show driver reloaded but an nvme errors line — opening a ticket with hw vendor.
Mira: reassigning next oncall for evening: Mira will take postmortem ownership and coord with infra for hardware diag.
Mira: handoff checklist -> capture full nvml topo + nvidia-smi -q outputs, collect kernel crash dumps from /var/crash, confirm driver version compatibility with runtime (containerd+cuda toolkit), run stress test on nodes 43/44 before rejoining pool.
Alex: also add canary traffic test: join node back cordoned, run small canary traffic with controlled model generation. If no errors for 30m, uncordon. document step commands.
Oncall-1: rejoining plan executed: performed `taint remove` after successful NVML checks on infer-node-43. canary run passed (30m, no Xid). uncordoned infer-node-43 at 13:05Z.
Oncall-1: infer-node-44 still flaky — infra continuing diagnostics. currently cordoned and marked NoSchedule.
deploy-bot: Routing: fallback model policy disabled once p99 lat stabilized. routing normalized by 13:20Z.
Support-Bot: CS notified customers of transient reroutes and mitigation steps. no escalations yet.
Mira: logging for postmortem — tagging incident with label: cause: hardware-driver, scope: inference-pool, severity: sev2, owners: Mira/Alex/Kevin/Jaya.
Alex: assigning postmortem to Mira, please include timeline, root cause analysis, action items (firmware update plan, driver auto-restart thresholds, hardware replacement if vendor confirms defect).
Mira: noted. will coordinate with infra to schedule firmware/drivers off-hours patch and add automated early-detection alert for Xid > 50 rates.
Kevin: any outstanding customer-facing actions?
Support-Bot: monitoring tickets; CS will provide proactive update if any customer asks.
Oncall-1: leaving detailed runbook steps in incident doc — will paste commands and logs there. handing off to Mira for post-incident follow-up.
Mira: taking it. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
